question_text: A legal-document summarisation feature must produce highly deterministic, repeatable outputs for the same input so that reviewers see consistent results. Which inference parameter setting best supports this requirement?

options.text: Set temperature near 0 (e.g. 0.0-0.2) to minimise randomness
Set temperature to 1.0 for balanced creativity
Increase top-K to the maximum allowed value
Remove the maxTokens limit entirely

explanation: Low temperature makes token selection near-greedy, producing deterministic, repeatable output ideal for factual/legal summarisation. Temperature 1.0 increases variability; a high top-K widens the candidate token pool and adds diversity; removing maxTokens affects length, not determinism.
source_topic: Temperature and sampling parameters for deterministic output

question_text: Which pair of inference parameters both influence the randomness/diversity of an FM's token selection (as opposed to output length)?

options.text: Temperature
Top-P (nucleus sampling)
maxTokens
Stop sequences

explanation: Temperature and Top-P both control the randomness/diversity of token sampling. maxTokens caps output length, and stop sequences halt generation at specific strings — neither changes the sampling distribution's diversity.

question_text: A downstream service must parse the FM's response programmatically. The model occasionally wraps its JSON in prose ("Here is your answer: {...}"), breaking the parser. Which approach most reliably forces clean, schema-conformant structured output?

options.text: Define the required JSON schema in the prompt and use the Converse API tool-use / structured output to constrain the response
Raise temperature so the model is more creative with formatting
Ask the model politely to 'try to return JSON'
Increase maxTokens so the JSON is never truncated

explanation: Providing an explicit JSON schema and using the Converse API's tool-use/structured-output mechanism constrains the model to emit only schema-conformant JSON, eliminating wrapper prose. Higher temperature worsens formatting consistency; a vague polite request is unreliable; more tokens prevents truncation but not prose wrapping.
source_topic: Structured output with JSON schema via Converse API

question_text: An enterprise needs an audit trail of who changed each production prompt and the ability to roll back to a previously approved version. Which Amazon Bedrock capability directly provides this?

options.text: Bedrock Prompt Management versioning combined with CloudTrail logging of prompt changes
Storing prompts as plain strings in Lambda environment variables
Hard-coding prompts in application source only
Setting a higher guardrail content-filter threshold

explanation: Bedrock Prompt Management versions every prompt edit and integrates with CloudTrail so changes are auditable and rollback to an approved version is possible. Lambda env vars and hard-coded prompts provide no FM-native versioning or approval audit; guardrail thresholds are a safety control, not prompt governance.
source_topic: Bedrock Prompt Management versioning and audit

question_text: A support assistant keeps drifting off-role after several conversation turns, occasionally answering questions outside its domain. Which practice most improves adherence to its defined role across a long conversation?

options.text: Place clear, specific role and boundary instructions in the system prompt and keep them present for every turn
Only include the role instruction in the very first user message
Lower maxTokens so the model cannot elaborate
Increase temperature to make responses more varied

explanation: The system prompt carries persistent behavioural instructions applied on every turn; making role and boundaries explicit there sustains adherence across long conversations. A first-user-turn instruction can be overridden by later turns; reducing maxTokens only truncates output; higher temperature increases drift.
source_topic: System prompt persistence for role adherence

question_text: A single support-response template must be reused across three product lines by substituting the product name and tone at runtime. Which Bedrock Prompt Management feature enables this without duplicating the template?

options.text: Prompt variables (named placeholders filled at invocation time)
Provisioned throughput
Cross-region inference
Guardrail denied topics

explanation: Prompt variables let one template accept named placeholders (e.g. {{product}}, {{tone}}) substituted at invocation time, so a single template serves many contexts. Provisioned throughput and cross-region inference are capacity/routing features; denied topics are a safety control.

question_text: Before promoting a modified prompt to production, a team wants to confirm it has not degraded answer quality on a fixed set of representative questions. Which practice achieves this?

options.text: Run the new prompt against a golden dataset and compare scores to the current baseline before deploying
Deploy directly to 100% of traffic and watch for complaints
Only test the new prompt with a single hand-picked easy question
Rely on temperature 0 to guarantee quality

explanation: Prompt regression testing runs a fixed golden dataset through the new prompt and compares quality scores against the established baseline, catching regressions before deployment. Full-traffic deployment risks user-facing degradation; a single easy question is not representative; temperature 0 controls determinism, not quality.
source_topic: Prompt regression testing with golden datasets

question_text: A workflow must classify an incoming request, then branch: factual queries go to a Knowledge Base retrieval step, creative queries go straight to generation, and off-topic queries get a refusal template. The team wants a low-code, visual way to build this on Bedrock. Which capability fits best?

options.text: Amazon Bedrock Prompt Flows with a condition node for branching
A single monolithic prompt with all logic inline
Amazon SQS fan-out
Amazon Bedrock Provisioned Throughput

explanation: Bedrock Prompt Flows provides a visual, low-code builder with input, prompt, Knowledge Base, condition (branching), and Lambda nodes — exactly matching classify-then-branch orchestration. A monolithic prompt is brittle and hard to maintain; SQS is a queue, not an FM orchestration builder; provisioned throughput is a capacity feature.

question_text: An extraction task must return entities in a precise, consistent format, but zero-shot prompting yields inconsistent field names and ordering. Which prompting technique most directly stabilises the output format?

options.text: Few-shot prompting — include 2-5 example input/output pairs showing the exact desired format
Raise temperature to encourage variety
Remove all instructions and let the model infer the format
Switch to a smaller, faster model

explanation: Few-shot prompting supplies concrete input/output examples that demonstrate the exact field names, ordering, and structure, strongly anchoring the model's output format. Higher temperature increases variability; removing instructions worsens consistency; model size does not by itself fix format drift.
source_topic: Few-shot prompting for consistent extraction format

question_text: Which instruction is the canonical way to elicit chain-of-thought reasoning from a foundation model on a multi-step problem?

options.text: "Let's think step by step" — instruct the model to show intermediate reasoning before the final answer
"Answer in one word only"
"Ignore all prior context"
"Respond with the highest temperature"

explanation: Chain-of-thought is elicited by asking the model to reason step by step, exposing intermediate steps that improve accuracy on multi-step tasks. A one-word instruction suppresses reasoning; ignoring context harms grounding; temperature is a numeric parameter, not a prompt instruction that produces reasoning.

question_text: A multi-turn chatbot must persist conversation history across sessions so a returning user's context is available, with low-latency reads keyed by session ID. Which AWS service is the most appropriate store for this session state?

options.text: Amazon DynamoDB keyed by session ID
Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive
An OpenSearch vector index of raw turns
CloudWatch Logs

explanation: DynamoDB provides low-latency, key-value access ideal for storing and retrieving conversation state by session ID. Glacier Deep Archive has retrieval latencies of hours; a vector index is for semantic search, not session state; CloudWatch Logs is for observability, not application state reads.

question_text: A user query is ambiguous ("book it for tomorrow" — book what?). Instead of guessing, the assistant should ask a follow-up question. Which prompt-engineering practice implements this behaviour?

options.text: Instruct the model in the system prompt to ask a clarifying question when the request is ambiguous or missing required parameters
Always assume the most likely intent and proceed without asking
Return an empty response for ambiguous input
Lower maxTokens so the model cannot ask questions

explanation: A clarification workflow is enforced via system-prompt instructions directing the model to request missing details before acting, reducing wrong actions on ambiguous input. Guessing risks incorrect outcomes; empty responses are poor UX; reducing maxTokens does not create clarification behaviour.

question_text: A GenAI feature must solve complex planning problems (e.g. multi-constraint scheduling) where a single linear chain-of-thought often commits early to a bad path and cannot recover. Which prompting technique explicitly explores multiple reasoning branches and evaluates them before selecting a final answer?

options.text: Tree-of-Thought — generate and evaluate multiple reasoning paths, then choose the most promising branch
Zero-shot prompting with a higher maxTokens limit
Few-shot prompting with two examples
Increasing temperature to 1.0 for more creative single answers

explanation: Tree-of-Thought (ToT) extends chain-of-thought by branching into several candidate reasoning paths, scoring/evaluating them, and pursuing the best — ideal for complex problems with multiple viable approaches where a single linear chain can commit to a dead end. Zero-shot with more tokens is still one linear path; few-shot supplies format examples but not multi-path exploration; raising temperature just adds randomness to one path.

question_text: A math/logic assistant using chain-of-thought sometimes produces a wrong final answer because a single reasoning trace makes an arithmetic slip. Without changing the model, which prompting strategy improves reliability by reducing the impact of any one faulty trace?

options.text: Self-consistency — sample multiple independent chain-of-thought responses and take the majority-vote answer
Set temperature to 0 and generate exactly one response
Remove the chain-of-thought instruction to shorten output
Add more denied topics to the guardrail

explanation: Self-consistency generates several independent reasoning paths (with some sampling temperature) and selects the most frequent final answer, so a single slip is outvoted by the correct majority — measurably improving accuracy on reasoning tasks. Temperature 0 with one response gives no diversity to vote over; removing CoT hurts reasoning quality; guardrail denied topics are a safety control, unrelated to arithmetic reliability.
